issue.title: [Alpha 44][Router] Parenthesis in urls
issue.body:
I have a problem with parenthesis characters:
`this.router.navigate(['./Show', {id: "The Player (2015)"]);`
---> works on first try
---> doesn't work on page refresh returns "The Player " (instead of "The Player (2015)")

And when I try to URI encode them:
`this.router.navigate(['./Show', {id: encodeURIComponent("The Player (2015)")]);`
---> doesn't works on first try (route params return "The%20Player%20")
---> doesn't work on page refresh returns "The%20Player%20" (instead of "The%20Player%20(2015)")

I guess that the problem is that the router will think that those parenthesis are auxiliary routes when you refresh the app. The router should probably encode those to something else and decode them for the params.
I'll make that myself for now, but it would probably be a good idea to have this implemented within the router himself for all "special" characters that it might use. I shouldn't be limited in any way regarding the characters that I put into the url.

body: Can you reopen this one please @alexeagle ? @vicb just closed the other issue

I'm having a similar issue with route params.  I'm passing as a parameter a Forex currency code.  E.g. "USD/GBP" - this is being passed to the router un-encoded and so it tries to route to /routename/USD/GBP

I definitely second this, and consider it quite high priority. If I send an arbitrary string in a routerLink, it should arrive as parameter in the route component, without caveats.
Otherwise, it is impossible to reliably use route parameters for any kind of user-supplied data, which severely cripples the potential use cases for the router.

This is really a show stopper when attempting to utilize the URI for state, e.g. example.com/(sessionid) => www.example.com/ Cannot match any routes: 'sessionid' (it removes the parenthesis from the error).  Any ETA would be very helpful to at least notify my manager of this issue.
What I started doing is using [ and ] instead of ( and ). The problem now is that release version encodes the url.
`( & )` are used for matrix params, you need to urlencode them if you need to use them.

That makes sense, but the problem is then with routerLink, which does not encode parenthesis, but _do_ encode other special characters (including %).
So it results in a double encoding if we manually encode the parenthesis before using them as parameters in a routerLink, or a broken route if we don't.

I have ran into this bug as well. The router cannot parse URLs with a matrix parameter containing `(` or `)` in its value. Replacing them with `%28` and `%29` respectively fixes the problem invoking the application but when navigating inside the application and setting such a parameter, the characters remain unquoted.

I find this rather problematic because I couldn't come up with a good workaround. As soon as the `(` etc. appears in the browser's URL bar, I have a link that cannot be copied and pasted.
